definitions.explanation: The residence of the Emperor of Japan, located in central Tokyo on the former site of Edo Castle. The grounds include the palace buildings, gardens, and a wide moat. Also used generically to refer to any emperor's palace.

examples.japanese: {皇居|こうきょ}の{周|まわ}りをジョギングした。
examples.english: I jogged around the Imperial Palace.

examples.japanese: {皇居|こうきょ}{東御苑|ひがしぎょえん}は{無料|むりょう}で{見学|けんがく}できる。
examples.english: The Imperial Palace East Gardens can be visited for free.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}の{一般|いっぱん}{参賀|さんが}では、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{皇居|こうきょ}を{訪|おとず}れて{天皇|てんのう}{陛下|へいか}のお{言葉|ことば}を{聞|き}く。
examples.english: During the New Year's public audience, many people visit the Imperial Palace to hear the Emperor's address.

notes:
LOCATION:
The {皇居|こうきょ} sits on approximately 115 hectares in the heart of Tokyo, surrounded by moats and stone walls from the original Edo Castle. The {皇居|こうきょ} {周回|しゅうかい}コース (Imperial Palace loop, approximately 5 km) is one of Tokyo's most popular jogging routes.

ACCESS:
The main palace grounds are generally closed to the public, but the {東御苑|ひがしぎょえん} (East Gardens) are open for free visits. The inner grounds open to the public twice a year: on the Emperor's birthday and January 2nd ({一般|いっぱん}{参賀|さんが}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {皇居|こうきょ}ランニング: running around the Imperial Palace
- {皇居|こうきょ}{周辺|しゅうへん}: Imperial Palace vicinity
- {皇居|こうきょ}{前|まえ}{広場|ひろば}: Imperial Palace front plaza
